analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: one big trade?
key_insights: US stocks are trading definitively lower on Thursday 22 October 2026 as the latest rise in oil prices is sparking more growth concerns than inflation concerns, and focus on the sustainability of the AI infrastructure trade intensifies in 3Q earnings season.
META, SPCX and TSLA have reported; MSFT, AMZN and GOOGL report next week.

AI spending news this week has been fairly encouraging: SPCX reported extremely strong results in its data center division and META highlighted the strength of its Agentic AI app Muse, giving investors some evidence of a return on AI investment.

AI complex companies face a high bar: investors want evidence that AI infrastructure investment is still growing (supporting data center demand and pricing power) and that the investments are yielding improving returns.
A chip shortage has been driving up data center prices, and one solution is more manufacturing capacity, which is where semi cap equipment stocks come in.

LRCX reported strong results and in-line 4Q guidance with bullish WFE commentary for 2027. It said 10 new semiconductor factories are scheduled to come online in 2027, a $200bn opportunity for the company.
LRCX shares are down 10% on the day despite the report, which GS ties to stock set-up. They are still up 37% YTD after the fall.
GS says LRCX's reaction is a reminder that this is not a bear market: the S&P 500 is up 12% YTD even after today's pullback, the 4th straight year of double-digit returns for the index.

SPOT delivered an in-line-to-positive quarter, with revenue, premium subs, MAUs, gross margin and operating income at or around guided levels, while continuing to invest in marketing, cloud/AI, audiobooks and AI-driven platform changes.

TMO beat and raised, with organic revenue growth of +6% led by LPS, Pharma Services, CRO and China. DHR beat EPS, derisked respiratory assumptions and cited 4-5% as a starting point for 2027 ex-respiratory growth. Both pointed to improving end markets into 2027.

BX had a 3Q26 discretionary earnings beat but missed on fee revenue per share, with the Real Estate management fee dragging and a weaker outlook for that division, offsetting stronger Credit & Insurance and Multi-Asset fundraising. NDAQ showed stronger momentum across FinTech, positive operating leverage and continued capital return.

PG posted a strong FQ1 beat with organic sales growth of +4.0% but largely maintained FY27 organic sales and core EPS guidance, citing commodity, energy, transportation, FX and macro concerns. TSCO beat on EPS and sales with comparable store sales +0.4% and FY26 guidance reiterated, but gross margin declined on higher transport and fuel costs.

LMT beat on revenue, adjusted EBIT, EPS and FCF, raised 2026 FCF guidance to $7.8-8.0bn and announced a 10-year F-35 framework agreement covering 850 US aircraft, contingent on Congressional multiyear procurement authority. HON results were solid and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $8.40-$8.45.
TSLA showed good progress in FSD and robotaxi, with strong Auto and Energy backlog and gross margin upside, but progress on the Optimus humanoid robot was not as strong in the quarter.

Initial jobless claims for the week ending October 17 fell 6k to 194k and continuing claims rose 25k to 1,728k. GS says labor data suggest domestic labor durability, keeping market pricing tilted toward potential Fed tightening later this year.

Chart of the Day (Joseph Briggs): under GS's forecast of a 15% productivity increase from AI, about 9% of workers could be temporarily displaced during the transition. Job losses drive employment reductions more than slower hiring, so AI-related layoffs should be a good real-time guide, and industry and occupation analyses suggest upside risks to labor disruption.

GS finds a positive, statistically significant correlation between AI adoption and unemployment in the service sector, while the correlation between AI adoption and job growth has turned slightly negative but is not statistically significant.
Midday performance at 12:17 PM: S&P 500 -1.0% on the day, DJIA 0.0%, NASDAQ -2.0%, Russell 2000 -0.0%.

risk_factors: Rising oil prices are sparking more growth concerns than inflation concerns.
The sustainability of the AI infrastructure trade is in question, and companies in the AI complex face a high bar for fundamentals and for evidence of returns on investment.
Elevated stock set-ups mean strong results can still produce sharp declines, as with LRCX.
Upside risks to AI-related labor disruption in the service sector, with about 9% of workers potentially temporarily displaced.
Higher transport and fuel costs are pressuring gross margins (TSCO) and weighing on PG's outlook alongside commodity, energy, FX and macro concerns.
LMT's F-35 framework agreement is contingent on Congressional multiyear procurement authority.
Market pricing leans toward Fed tightening later this year given labor durability.
